rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): suppress native browser context menu
rawCommits.body:
Right-clicking empty AURA chrome was showing the WebView2 / Chromium
native menu (Back, Refresh, Save as, Print, More tools, Inspect),
breaking the desktop OS feel. Install a single document-level listener
that defers to any in-app onContextMenu (DesktopContextMenu,
NotesEntryContextMenu, ProcessCanvas, ...) via event.defaultPrevented,
and otherwise cancels the native menu. Inside editable text fields
(input, textarea, contenteditable) we replace the native menu with a
compact in-app Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All so right-click editing
still works without giving up control of the chrome.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): widen top-edge resize hit area on Windows
rawCommits.body:
The borderless main window inherits tao's default WM_NCHITTEST
behavior, which only reports HTTOP within SM_CYFRAME (~4 logical
px) of the top edge. Combined with the floating titlebar pill
that begins 5 px below the window edge, hitting the resize zone
required pixel-perfect aim.

Install a Win32 subclass on the main HWND that returns
HTTOP/HTTOPLEFT/HTTOPRIGHT for any cursor inside a 10-logical-px
band along the top, falling through to DefSubclassProc for every
other position so titlebar drag, side resize, and Chromium
app-region all keep working unchanged. The subclass is dispatched
before tao's by virtue of being installed last, becomes a no-op
while the window is maximized, and re-reads DPI on each hit-test
so it stays consistent across mixed-DPI monitor setups.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: widen top-edge resize hit area on Windows

rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): defer-open pattern for async-loading modals
rawCommits.body:
When the user clicked Delete on an agent attached to multiple
projects, the confirm modal opened immediately, then janked: the
"Delete" button widened to "Delete and remove from N projects" and
a cascade-warning paragraph appeared once bindings finished loading.
Same flicker existed for the marketplace Hire modal (in-modal
spinner -> project list) and the Tier subscription modal ("Loading
plan details..." -> tier grid).

Introduce useDeferredModalOpen, a tiny shared hook that runs the
caller's prepare() (e.g. cascade.refresh / projectsStore.refresh /
billingStore.fetchSubscription), keeps the modal closed and shows a
disabled trigger button until the prepare resolves, and only then
flips isOpen true. A 3000ms failsafe opens the modal even if prepare
never settles. Stale resolutions from a previous open cycle are
ignored via an internal cycle token.

Apply to three call sites:
- DeleteAgentConfirmModal (AgentList + AgentInfoPanel) - also shorten
  the cascade label from "Delete and remove from N projects" to
  "Delete (N projects)" so width is stable across binding counts.
- HireProjectPickerModal (MarketplaceMainPanel) - drop the in-modal
  spinner; the per-card Hire button disables briefly while preparing.
- TierSubscriptionModal (OrgSettingsPanel via OrgSettingsRewards /
  OrgSettingsBilling) - read subscription from billing-store instead
  of fetching on open; the Upgrade / Change Plan trigger disables
  briefly while preparing.

The remaining modals from the audit (AgentSelectorModal,
BuyCreditsModal, ProjectSettingsModal, etc.) are deliberately left
for follow-up PRs - the shared hook is the substrate for those.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: defer-open pattern for async-loading modals

rawCommits.subject: feat: split AURA into dev and stable build channels
rawCommits.body:
Introduce a build-time channel selector on aura-os-core
(`stable-channel` default, `dev-channel` opt-in via cargo features)
so a `cargo run`-built dev AURA can run side-by-side with the
installed stable AURA on one machine without colliding on data
dirs, ports, single-instance locks, skills trees, or window
identity. Remote services stay shared via .env.

The new `Channel` enum in `aura-os-core::channel` is the single
source of truth for every per-channel identifier: data dir name
(`aura` vs `aura-dev`), skills home (`~/.aura` vs `~/.aura-dev`),
Windows single-instance mutex, window/menu title, embedded
desktop server port (19847 vs 19848), standalone server port
(3100 vs 3101), harness sidecar port (19080 vs 19081), default
harness URL port (8080 vs 8081), and updater enablement (off in
dev so a cargo-built shell can never silently replace itself
with the stable installer).

`cargo run -p aura-os-desktop` and the `scripts/dev/*` runners
default to the dev channel via cargo's default feature. The
release pipeline (`cargo packager`, `verify-desktop.mjs`, the
`release-stable` and `release-nightly` workflows) builds with
`--no-default-features --features stable-channel`. The desktop
crate disables default features on its `aura-os-core` and
`aura-os-server` deps so a stable packaging build cannot
accidentally pull in `dev-channel` from a transitive default.

Dev script defaults bumped to dev-channel ports (Vite 5174,
mobile backend 3101) so a developer running `npm run dev` or the
mobile runner does not bind on top of an installed stable AURA.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: split AURA into dev and stable build channels

rawCommits.subject: fix(agents): recognize renamed CEO via system-prompt prefix
rawCommits.body:
After renaming the bootstrap CEO (e.g. "CEO" -> "Maia") and re-logging
in, the server was creating a duplicate "CEO" agent. `looks_like_ceo`
only recognised renamed CEOs via the locally-stamped
`bootstrap:ceo_agent_id` setting or an exact name+role both equal to
"CEO". CEOs created before commit 2dabef61a (the stamping fix) never
had the local stamp, so a post-rename login fell through both checks
and `dedupe_ceo_agents` returned no canonical, causing
`setup_ceo_agent` to mint a fresh duplicate.

Add a third identity signal: the canonical CEO `system_prompt` prefix
("You are the CEO SuperAgent"), extracted into a shared constant so
the matcher and the template stay in lock-step. The agent editor
preserves `system_prompt` on save unless the user explicitly rewrites
it, so this prefix survives a rename and lets the dedupe step pick the
older renamed CEO as canonical and best-effort delete the freshly-
minted duplicate on the next setup call.

Adds four unit tests: renamed-name-only, full rename, arbitrary system
prompt is not a CEO, and a drift guard that `ceo_system_prompt()`
always starts with `CEO_SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(interface): suppress focus-visible outline on dialog/modal wrappers
rawCommits.body:
Container elements with `tabindex="-1"`, `role="dialog"`, or
`aria-modal="true"` are focused programmatically for keyboard /
screen-reader scope management, not as tab stops. When the user pressed
Shift (or Shift+Tab) Chromium flipped into keyboard-modality, and the
zui Modal's `modalRef.current?.focus()` call on its `tabIndex={-1}`
wrapper triggered the global `:focus-visible` rule and painted a 2px
white ring around the entire modal box. Extend the existing
`#root` / `.titlebar-drag` opt-out to also cover those container
patterns (and both `:focus` and `:focus-visible` for keyboard-modality
edge cases) so high-level wrappers never paint a focus ring while real
interactive controls keep their accessible focus indicator.

This fixes the "I had to close the app and come back to see the scene"
symptom. The previous fix added `generate_3d_model` to
`AUTO_EXPAND_TOOLS`, but `defaultActivitiesExpanded` is only true for
the just-finalized bubble — once `ChatMessageList`'s `justFinalizedIdRef`
clears (any navigation away or app remount), the bubble re-rendered
collapsed and hid the embedded viewer. Bypassing the Block on success
makes the widget render unconditionally so the scene shows up
immediately in the current chat session, and stays visible after
remount. The auto-expand entry is no longer needed and is removed.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: render scene as standalone widget (no Block wrapper)

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat-sessions): unify sidekick session list and default to most recent
rawCommits.body:
Both apps now use one shared `SessionsList` component (date-bucketed
buttons, summaries, selected-row highlight). Clicking a session in the
project sidekick now navigates the main chat to that session — the row
click was previously unwired. The chat view auto-redirects to the most
recent session by `started_at` when the URL has no `?session=` and no
live-session pin, in both the project route and the agents-shell
standalone route.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: unify sidekick session list and default to most recent

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): unify session-list state in zustand store, fix infinite-loop crash
rawCommits.body:
The previous unification commit shipped a `selectAgentBindings` selector
that returned a fresh `{ projectId, agentInstanceId }` array on every
call. `useShallow` compares array items by reference, so each render
saw "new" objects, committed, re-rendered, and looped — surfacing as
"Maximum update depth exceeded" the moment any agent chat mounted on
`/agents/:agentId` without a session in the URL. Conversations stopped
loading entirely.

Replace the ad-hoc selector with a single `useSessionsListStore` that
owns `sessionsBySurface` keyed by `agent:{agentId}` /
`project:{projectId}`, plus `loadAgentSessions`, `loadProjectSessions`,
optimistic `removeSession` / `restoreSession`, and per-surface
request-id race protection. Both default-session redirects, the agents
`ChatsTab`, and the projects `SessionList` now read from this one
source of truth — no more duplicated fetches and no more derived-array
selectors.

While here:
- Drop the `agent` / `projectBindings` props on `ChatsTab`; pull from
  `useSelectedAgent()` and a stable `useAgentBindingsKey` string
  fingerprint instead.
- Drop the redundant 5-second poll in `useSessionListData`; the
  existing `version` bump on `SessionReady` and the new-chat path
  drives reads.
- Add regression tests for selector identity stability, store
  request-id ordering, and no-infinite-loop on standalone redirect.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: unify session-list state in zustand store, fix infinite-loop crash

rawCommits.subject: fix(release): build packaged desktop binary with stable-channel feature
rawCommits.body:
The two-job release pipeline (build-app -> package) never activated the
stable-channel cargo feature, so every published "stable" / "nightly"
installer shipped the dev-channel binary: window/taskbar title was
"AURA Dev", per-user data lived in `aura-dev` instead of `aura`, dev
ports were used, and the in-app updater was silently disabled
(updater_enabled() is false for Dev). The build-app job ran
`cargo build --release --package aura-os-desktop`, which picks up
aura-os-desktop's default `dev-channel` features. The package job then
strips `before-packaging-command` from Cargo.toml (to avoid a duplicate
prebuild) and packages the prebuilt binary verbatim via the
`binaries-dir = "../../prebuilt-binaries"` injection.

Add `--no-default-features --features stable-channel` to the
`Build release binary` step in both release workflows so the artifact
that gets packaged actually compiles as Stable. Also rewrite the
misleading `Package installer` comment in both files (and the matching
one in desktop-validate.yml) which still claimed the channel feature
was wired in via `before-packaging-command` even though that line is
deleted earlier in the same job.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: build packaged desktop binary with stable-channel feature

rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): embed AURA icon into Windows .exe PE resources
rawCommits.body:
Start Menu, File Explorer, "pin to taskbar" tile, and Alt+Tab fallback
all read the icon from disk (via the .lnk shortcut or the .exe's first
RT_GROUP_ICON resource). The runtime tao::WindowBuilder::with_window_icon
HICON only covers the live taskbar of the running window, so without an
embedded resource Windows fell back to the generic blue/white executable
glyph everywhere else.

Wire winresource into apps/aura-os-desktop/build.rs (Windows-only build
dep) and compile assets/installer/installer-icon.ico - already generated
as a multi-size 16/32/48/64/128/256 ICO by
infra/scripts/icons/generate-app-icons.mjs - into the produced binary,
along with ProductName/FileDescription/CompanyName/LegalCopyright strings
so Task Manager and the .exe properties dialog stop showing the bare
crate name. Compile failures (e.g. missing llvm-rc on a cross host) emit
a cargo:warning instead of panicking so local non-Windows builds keep
working.

Verified by rebuilding aura-os-desktop and extracting the icon from the
release .exe (32x32 AURA orb) and inspecting VersionInfo via
Get-Item.VersionInfo.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: embed AURA icon into Windows .exe PE resources

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat-sessions): make historical sessions editable, URL is source of truth
rawCommits.body:
Clicking a session in the agents/projects sidekick now opens it as a
live, editable thread instead of a read-only banner view: the next
message extends the existing session with the correct historical
context. The "+" chat-input button drops the URL `?session=` and
clears the visible transcript so the next send creates a fresh
session server-side; SessionReady mirrors the new id back into the
URL so it stays the single source of truth.

Backend
- Add `session_id: Option<String>` to `SendChatRequest`.
- New `try_pin_session` validates the pin against the agent's session
  list and returns a typed `PinnedSessionOutcome`. Mismatches surface
  as a structured 400 (`session_id ... does not belong to agent ...`)
  instead of silently writing into the wrong thread.
- `resolve_chat_session_with_pin` honors the pin (force_new wins);
  `setup_*_chat_persistence` and `load_*_session_events_for_*` accept
  the pin so persistence and LLM context come from the same session.
- Live harness session is force-evicted when the pin disagrees with
  the resident `ChatSession.session_id`, otherwise switching sessions
  would keep the old conversation hot in memory.

Frontend
- Delete `useLiveSessionStore`. Replace its pinning with an
  `onSessionReady(id)` callback wired into `useChatStream` /
  `useAgentChatStream`; the chat panel writes `?session=<id>` into
  the URL via `setSearchParams({ replace: true })`.
- `AgentChatView` (project + standalone branches) drops
  `SessionBanner`, `noopSend`, and the `isSessionView` read-only
  branch -- `historyKey` is just `session:...` when pinned, send is
  always real, and the `+` button clears `?session=` rather than
  hitting the reset endpoint.
- Default-session redirects no longer take a `liveSessionId` --
  cold-opening `/agents/:agentId` (or the project equivalent) drops
  you on the most recent editable session, ChatGPT-style.

Tests
- New `pin_tests` cover NotRequested / Matched / Mismatch and the
  force_new-overrides-pin path.
- Frontend stream tests assert the new 11th `sessionId` arg.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: make historical sessions editable, URL is source of truth

rawCommits.subject: fix(terminal): keep xterm palette in sync with theme toggle
rawCommits.body:
XTerminal's resolvedTheme effect ran before ZUI ThemeProvider's effect
that flips <html data-theme>, so getXtermTheme's getComputedStyle read
the previous palette and the terminal background lagged the rest of the
chrome by one toggle. Observe data-theme directly via MutationObserver
to decouple from React effect ordering.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep xterm palette in sync with theme toggle

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): clear stream slot when navigating between sessions
rawCommits.body:
Clicking a different session in the sidekick was leaving the previous
session's events visible in the main panel. The hydrate-to-stream
guard in `useChatHistorySync` skips the reset whenever
`streamCount >= historyMessages.length` (a defense against blinking
the just-finished stream while history catches up mid-turn), so the
old session's events stayed pinned until something pushed a new
event in.

Both chat panels now explicitly clear the stream slot whenever the
URL `?session=` flips. The mid-turn `null -> defined` transition
(from the post-send `SessionReady` URL update) is excluded so a
fresh-canvas first send doesn't wipe its own in-flight events.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: clear stream slot when navigating between sessions

rawCommits.subject: fix(terminal): match xterm bg to surrounding pane in both themes
rawCommits.body:
The terminal palette in tokens.css hardcoded `--color-terminal-bg`
(and `--color-terminal-cursor-accent`) to `#1e1e1e` (dark) / `#ffffff`
(light), but the TerminalPanel container itself paints `var(--color-bg)`
(`#09090b` in dark, `#ffffff` in light). In dark mode the difference
showed up as a visibly lighter rectangle wherever the embedded terminal
was mounted (sidekick terminal, project terminal pane, etc.).

Alias `--color-terminal-bg` and `--color-terminal-cursor-accent` to
`var(--color-bg)` in both `[data-theme='dark']` and `[data-theme='light']`
so xterm renders flush with the pane chrome and follows any
user-customized `--color-bg` from theme overrides. The other terminal
tokens (foreground, ANSI palette, selection) keep their VS Code-derived
values.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: match xterm bg to surrounding pane in both themes

rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): widen top window resize hit zone to 14px
rawCommits.body:
The 10px Win32 WM_NCHITTEST band on the main window's top edge was
hard to grab reliably. Bump TOP_RESIZE_BORDER_LOGICAL_PX to 14 so the
top edge resizes comfortably; pill button centerline clicks remain
unaffected and existing chrome tests still pass.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: widen top window resize hit zone to 14px

rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): clean session sidekick labels and show new sessions immediately
rawCommits.body:
The sidekick had two display bugs that landed together after the
session-continuation refactor:

- The Haiku summarizer was unconstrained, so persisted summaries
  occasionally started with `# Session Summary` / `**Title**` /
  list markers, which leaked through verbatim into the chats list.
- Any session whose `summary_of_previous_context` was still empty
  was hidden entirely while Haiku ran, so a brand-new `+`-button
  session sat invisible for the 1-3s round-trip and the panel
  showed "No sessions yet" mid-conversation.

Render-time fix in `session-row-utils.ts` strips ATX headings,
blockquotes, list markers, and wrapping bold/italic/code from the
first visible line, so existing summaries in the database render
cleanly without a backfill. The Haiku system prompt is also
tightened to forbid markdown going forward.

`deriveSessionLabel` now returns a non-null `"New chat"` placeholder
when no summary is available, and `SessionsList` drops the
null-skip so every session in the API response renders immediately.
`useSessionSummaries` upgrades the label in place when Haiku
returns. After the lazy-`+` refactor, every row in
`listProjectSessions` already has at least one user message, so
there are no "truly empty" sessions to filter out.

Adds `session-row-utils.test.ts` with regressions for the markdown
strip, the placeholder fallback, and the upgrade-in-place flow.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: clean session sidekick labels and show new sessions immediately

rawCommits.subject: fix(mode-selector): keep textarea focused when clicking mode pills
rawCommits.body:
Calling preventDefault on the segment button's mousedown stops the pill
from grabbing focus from the chat textarea below it, so switching
between Code / Plan / Image / 3D no longer defocuses the input. Click
selection and arrow-key navigation are unaffected.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep textarea focused when clicking mode pills

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): defer standalone panel mount during agent switch
rawCommits.body:
Clicking another agent in the sidebar navigates to `/agents/B` with no
session params, so `AgentChatView` was mounting `StandaloneAgentChatPanel`
for one render cycle, firing its per-agent timeline fetch, and then
unmounting it as soon as `useDefaultStandaloneSessionRedirect` pushed
`?project=&instance=&session=` into the URL and `ProjectAgentChatPanel`
took over with a different `streamKey`. The two back-to-back cold-load
reveals produced the agent-switch flicker.

Gate the standalone arm on a "redirect not imminent" signal computed
synchronously from `sessions-list-store` + `useAgentBindingsKey`. While
the redirect is pending (bindings exist and either sessions are cached
or the surface hasn't been loaded yet), render a stable lane-coloured
placeholder so only `ProjectAgentChatPanel` mounts. Agents with no
bindings or with an empty sessions surface still render the standalone
panel immediately - no behaviour change for them.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: defer standalone panel mount during agent switch

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): wait for session events cache before mounting chat panel
rawCommits.body:
The previous fix suppressed the transient `StandaloneAgentChatPanel`
mount, but on the cold path the user still saw `ProjectAgentChatPanel`
mount with empty content while its per-session events fetch was in
flight - the chat structure (header, input bar) painted first and the
messages faded in on top.

Replace the boolean defer-redirect gate with `useAgentsShellTarget`,
a single resolver that:

- picks the target session synchronously (URL params, falling back to
  the agent's `mostRecent`),
- eagerly calls `chat-history-store.fetchHistory` for that session so
  `useChatHistorySync` finds the entry already in flight (or `ready`),
- keeps the lane placeholder up until the entry reports `ready`/`error`,
  AT WHICH POINT `ProjectAgentChatPanel` mounts hot - `historyResolved`
  is true on the first render so the cold-load overlay never trips and
  the transcript appears in one go.

Net result: clicking an agent goes lane background -> fully populated
chat, with no chat-shell flash in between, on both the warm path
(sessions cached) and the cold path (first-time fetch).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: wait for session events cache before mounting chat panel

rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): add JS top-resize bridge to actually widen the hit area
rawCommits.body:
The Win32 WM_NCHITTEST subclass on the parent HWND never fires for
cursor positions over the WebView2 child, which fills the entire
client area as a WS_CHILD that returns HTCLIENT. Bumping its band
constant in chrome.rs (10 -> 14 px) was effectively cosmetic — the
only place the subclass actually fires is the 1-logical-pixel
non-client strip tao reserves on the very top of the parent on
Windows 11 (0 px on Windows 10).

Mirror the existing native-titlebar-drag.ts approach: the web layer
DOES see pointer events even when the native child swallows them, so
install a document-level handler that paints `cursor: n-resize` while
the pointer sits in the top 14 logical px and IPCs `resize-n` on a
non-interactive primary-button pointerdown. A new
`WinCmd::Resize(ResizeDirection)` is wired through the event loop
(both main and secondary windows) to call
`tao::Window::drag_resize_window(North)`, handing off to the OS
native resize loop.

Refresh the doc comment over `TOP_RESIZE_BORDER_LOGICAL_PX` to be
honest about the subclass's limited reach. Keep the constant in sync
with the JS band so the corner kiss-zones the subclass reports
(HTTOPLEFT / HTTOPRIGHT) line up with the JS band's top edge.

Tests: 16 new vitest cases in native-titlebar-resize.test.ts cover
band geometry, interactive-target exclusion, cursor painting, and
the no-bridge no-op path. All 73 aura-os-desktop unit tests still
pass.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: add JS top-resize bridge to actually widen the hit area

rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): surface aura-storage errors when right-click delete fails
rawCommits.body:
`delete_session` was collapsing every non-404 from aura-storage into an
opaque `internal_error` 500 with no server-side log, and the FE only
`console.error`d before silently restoring the row — so right-click
"Delete session" appeared to do nothing whenever the upstream rejected
the DELETE.

Server: log the upstream status + body preview and reuse
`map_storage_error` so the real status (e.g. 409 / 502) flows through
to the response, matching how `get_session` and the other sibling
handlers already work. Adds a regression test that a 409 from the
upstream comes back as 409 instead of 500.

Frontend: thread a per-surface `deleteErrorBySurface` through
`useSessionsListStore`, surface it as a small dismissible alert at the
top of `SessionsList` (used by both the agents `ChatsTab` and the
projects `SessionList`), and format the message from `ApiClientError`
as "Couldn't delete session (status): server message".

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: surface aura-storage errors when right-click delete fails

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): stop wiping the stream on the post-SessionReady URL flip
rawCommits.body:
Tighten the panel session-transition effect so it only clears the
stream slot on a true cross-session navigation (defined to different
defined) when no turn is actively streaming, and skip the
invalidate-before-fetch step in `useChatHistorySync` while the
streamKey is live. Together these stop a fresh-canvas first send from
flashing `.messageContentHidden` over the optimistic user bubble (and
then clobbering the previous turn on the next send) once `SessionReady`
recomputes the panel's `historyKey`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stop wiping the stream on the post-SessionReady URL flip

rendered.title: Native chrome polish, editable chat sessions, and a real Stable channel
rendered.intro: A dense day for AURA: right-click finally feels native across the desktop, the chat sidekick gets a unified, editable session list with summarized titles, 3D chat lands as a true two-step image-then-model pipeline, and the release pipeline is rewired so installers actually ship the Stable channel binary. Plenty of Windows-specific polish too, from a wider top-edge resize zone to an embedded app icon.

entries.title: Right-click on AURA chrome stops opening the WebView2 menu
entries.summary: A document-level override replaces Chromium's native context menu with in-app behavior, restoring the desktop-OS feel.

items.text: Right-clicking empty AURA chrome no longer surfaces the WebView2 Back/Refresh/Inspect menu; in-app handlers like DesktopContextMenu and NotesEntryContextMenu are still respected via defaultPrevented.
Inside inputs, textareas, and contenteditable fields, right-click now opens a compact in-app Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All menu so editing keeps working without the native chrome.

entries.title: Easier top-edge window resizing on Windows
entries.summary: A Win32 subclass widens the resize hit zone along the top of the borderless main window so grabbing it no longer requires pixel-perfect aim.

items.text: On Windows, the main window now reports HTTOP/HTTOPLEFT/HTTOPRIGHT across a 10-logical-pixel band along the top edge, leaving titlebar drag, side resizes, and Chromium app-region behavior untouched.
The hit-test re-reads DPI on every event and becomes a no-op while the window is maximized, so behavior stays correct across mixed-DPI monitor setups.

entries.title: Modals wait for their data before opening
entries.summary: A new useDeferredModalOpen hook removes the jank where Delete Agent, Hire, and Tier modals would open empty and then reflow as data loaded.

items.text: DeleteAgentConfirmModal, HireProjectPickerModal, and TierSubscriptionModal now keep their trigger button briefly disabled while data loads and only open once content is ready, with a 3000ms failsafe so the modal can't get stuck closed.
The cascade label on Delete Agent is shortened from 'Delete and remove from N projects' to 'Delete (N projects)' so the button width stays stable regardless of binding count.

entries.title: Dev and stable AURA can now coexist on one machine
entries.summary: A new build-time channel selector gives the dev build its own data dir, ports, single-instance lock, and window identity so it no longer collides with an installed AURA.

items.text: aura-os-core gains a Channel enum that drives every per-channel identifier — data dir (aura vs aura-dev), skills home, Windows mutex, window/menu title, embedded server port (19847/19848), standalone server (3100/3101), harness sidecar (19080/19081), and updater enablement.

cargo run and the scripts/dev runners default to the dev channel, while release-stable and release-nightly workflows build with --no-default-features --features stable-channel so packaged installers stay on the stable identity.
The in-app updater is disabled in dev builds so a cargo-built shell can never silently replace the installed Stable binary.

entries.title: 3D chat mode returns with an image-first flow
entries.summary: The 3D pill is back in the chat mode selector, wired to generate an image first and then convert it, mirroring the standalone AURA 3D app.

items.text: The chat input derives its 3D source from the most recent successful generate_image tool result, surfaces it as a 'Source for 3D' thumbnail, and dispatches the request via generate3dStream's URL form; manual image attachments stay disabled until the proxy decode-and-forward path is fixed.
The AURA 3D app's Image tab no longer appends the product-photography STYLE_LOCK_SUFFIX to user prompts, so image generation now behaves consistently with /image and /3d.

entries.title: Editable chat sessions, native context menus, and Stable-channel installers
entries.summary: The evening's long batch reshapes the chat session model, finishes the native-feel context menu work, lands S3 image uploads, and fixes a string of Windows desktop and release-pipeline bugs.

items.text: The agents and projects sidekicks now share one SessionsList: rows are clickable, default to the most recent session, get Haiku-summarized titles (with markdown stripped from the labels), and surface real server errors when right-click delete fails. State is consolidated into a single useSessionsListStore, fixing a 'Maximum update depth exceeded' crash that had blocked agent chat from loading at all.

Historical sessions are now live, editable threads instead of read-only banners: a server-side session_id pin validates against the agent's session list, the URL becomes the source of truth via SessionReady, and the chat input '+' button starts a fresh session by clearing the URL. Several follow-ups stop the stream slot from flashing or wiping itself across session navigations and during agent switches.

Chat 3D is reworked into an in-bar two-step image-then-model pipeline: the source thumb moves inline with a removable pin, image-only sends now dispatch the 3D model step, and finished models render as a standalone WebGLViewer with a download link instead of a collapsed Block. The chat-only style-lock suffix is later removed entirely.

The native-feel context menu work expands: right-clicking selected text in markdown output now offers Copy, right-clicking an image offers Copy Image (re-encoding to PNG via canvas when needed), and the desktop background entry is shortened to 'Background'.

Image attachments now upload to S3 via a new presign proxy endpoint: the chat input blocks send while uploads are in flight, dims uploading thumbnails, and message bubbles render images directly from their S3 source_url through both the live stream and history paths.

Released installers finally ship as Stable: the build-app job now compiles aura-os-desktop with --no-default-features --features stable-channel, fixing 'AURA Dev' titles, the wrong data dir, dev ports, and a silently-disabled updater in shipped builds. An earlier flag mistake on cargo packager itself is also corrected.

On Windows, the AURA orb icon is embedded into the .exe's PE resources via winresource so Start Menu, File Explorer, taskbar pin, and Alt+Tab fallbacks stop showing the generic executable glyph; ProductName/FileDescription metadata is set too.

The top-edge resize zone is widened to 14 logical pixels and now actually fires over the WebView2 child via a JS bridge that paints n-resize and IPCs into a new WinCmd::Resize that calls tao's drag_resize_window — the original Win32 subclass alone couldn't reach the WebView's client area.

Chat scrolling now respects user intent: an explicit upward scroll suspends auto-follow until the user reaches the very bottom again, so streaming output and the post-stream image pin can no longer yank the viewport back down mid-read.

The feedback app gets a Notes-style sidekick split into Details and Comments tabs, and every new submission is auto-tagged with the active app version (rendered as a small vX.Y.Z chip on each card) so support can correlate reports with the exact build.

A duplicate 'CEO' agent could appear after renaming the bootstrap CEO and re-logging in; the matcher now also recognizes the canonical 'You are the CEO SuperAgent' system-prompt prefix so renamed CEOs survive dedupe.

Smaller interface polish: a jet-black modal background token with per-mode override in Settings > Appearance, inverted ZUI button dim so rest is full opacity and hover fades, the titlebar Update pill at full accent saturation, a 'New Agent' fallback for nameless sidebar rows, suppressed focus rings on dialog wrappers, redesigned empty-state prompt suggestions with a slower input pulse, a stable bottom-bar environment slot during agent switches, attaching an Orbit repo from the project settings modal, mode pills that no longer steal focus from the textarea, terminal palette that follows theme toggles in real time and matches the surrounding pane, and breathing room around chat image attachments.

highlights: Native browser context menu replaced with in-app menus across editable text, selections, and images
Chat sessions are now editable, summarized, and unified between the agents and projects sidekicks
3D chat mode rebuilt as an in-bar image-then-model pipeline with embedded GLB viewer
Stable installers now actually ship the stable-channel binary, with proper Windows icons embedded
New dev/stable channel split lets a cargo-built AURA run alongside the installed app
